lines: One randomly generated modulation source: each trigger starts a low-frequency oscillator at a random rate, waveform and phase, or replaces it with a single steady random voltage.
A rising edge generates a fresh random setting for every output.
Sets how far a generated setting may stray from BIAS; at 0 every trigger gives the same rate and the same held voltage, though the waveform is chosen afresh each time.
Sets the centre that the random rate and the random held voltage are drawn around, -1 to +1; at the middle the rate is drawn around 1Hz and held voltages around 0V.
In its upper position each trigger has an even chance of producing a steady held voltage instead of an oscillator; in its lower position every trigger produces an oscillator.
Switches the output between -5V to +5V in the lower position and 0V to 10V in the upper one, the upper setting adding 5V to whatever was generated.
The generated modulation, either a running oscillator or a steady held voltage.
Note — Nothing changes until a trigger reaches TRIG. VAR, BIAS and the S&H switch are read at the instant of the trigger, so turning them has no effect until the next one.
Note — An output's oscillator only advances while that jack is patched, so an unpatched output is frozen rather than running silently.
Note — A generated oscillator is a blend of sine, triangle, saw and square chosen at random, started at a random phase, at a random rate up to eight octaves either side of the BIAS centre.

lines: A mixer of up to eight inputs whose channel levels are drawn from simplex noise, so the blend drifts or jumps at random instead of being set by hand.
At ON TRIG the levels only change when a trigger arrives; at FREE they change continuously.
A rising edge picks a new set of channel levels while the switch is at ON TRIG.
One of the signals to be mixed; a channel is only given a level, and only reaches the mix, while its jack is patched.
Sets how fast the noise driving the levels moves, 0.005 at the left to 1 at the right.
Adds a tenth of its voltage to SPEED, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Sets how many octaves of noise are summed into the level movement, 1 for smooth movement through to 8 for movement full of small bumps.
Adds to JITTER, -5V adding nothing and +5V adding five; the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Multiplies the noise before it is clipped, 1 at the left to 10 at the right, so higher settings hold a channel fully open or fully shut for longer and cross between them faster.
The patched inputs added together at their current levels and divided by the sum of those levels, so the overall loudness stays near steady as the blend changes.
Note — The switch comes up at ON TRIG and every channel level starts at 0, so a newly placed module is silent until a trigger reaches TRIG or the switch is moved to FREE.
Note — A channel level runs from fully shut to fully open and never inverts the signal.
Note — The green lamp beside a channel shows that channel's present level.
Note — Only the first channel of a polyphonic cable is mixed.

lines: An audio oscillator whose single cycle is read out of a field of simplex noise, with a small display of the wave it is producing.
Toggles the waveform being mirrored at its halfway point, making each cycle symmetrical; the lamp is lit while mirroring is on and the setting is stored with the patch.
A rising edge toggles the mirroring from outside the module, with no need to press MIRROR.
Sets the pitch in volts, -3 to +3; 0V gives C4 at 261.63Hz.
Pitch at a volt per octave, added to FREQ; the number of channels patched here sets the oscillator's polyphony.
Shifts the pitch by up to half an octave either way.
Shifts the pitch by a fifth of an octave per volt, added to FINE.
Moves the start of the read across the noise field, 0 to 5, which gives a different waveform at every setting.
Adds a quarter of its voltage to X, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Moves the read to a different row of the noise field, 0 to 5, which gives an unrelated waveform at every setting.
Adds a quarter of its voltage to Y, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Sets how much of the noise field one cycle covers, 0.5 at the left to 5.5 at the right, so higher settings give a busier waveform.
Adds a quarter of its voltage to SCALE, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Sets how many octaves of noise are summed into the waveform, 1 for a plain shape through to 8 for one full of fine wrinkles.
Adds 0.8 to DETAIL per volt, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
A rising edge restarts the waveform from the beginning of its cycle.
A pulse one sample long at the end of each cycle: 11V with nothing patched to SYNC, and with SYNC patched 10V at a natural end of cycle and 11V on the sample a sync restarts the oscillator.
The waveform, rescaled so that the loudest and quietest values it has produced lately reach -5V and +5V.
Note — The output is normalised against the highest and lowest values in the last 2048 samples, rechecked every 256 samples, so the level stays near ±5V as the waveform is changed.
Note — An 11V pulse at the SYNC input restarts the display as well as the oscillator, which is what the 11V from this module's own EOC output is for; a 10V pulse restarts only the oscillator.
Note — The pitch from the two knobs and the two pitch inputs together is limited to three and a half octaves either side of C4.

lines: A three-oscillator wavetable oscillator that ships with no wavetable: you record one into it from three signal inputs, and it is then stored in the patch.

A rising edge starts a recording, with no need to press CAPTURE.
While this is patched a rising edge here starts the recording and the next edge ends it, so the table holds exactly one cycle of whatever oscillator is driving it.
The signal recorded into the wavetable's top waveform; the maker's tooltip calls all three capture jacks Top capture.
The signal recorded into the wavetable's middle waveform; the maker's tooltip calls all three capture jacks Top capture.
The signal recorded into the wavetable's bottom waveform; the maker's tooltip calls all three capture jacks Top capture.
Toggles every oscillator reading the table forwards and then backwards, so each cycle comes out symmetrical; the lamp is lit while that is on.
A rising edge toggles the mirroring, with no need to press the button.
Sets the main oscillator's pitch in volts, -3 to +3; 0V gives C4 at 261.63Hz.
Pitch at a volt per octave, added to FREQ; the number of channels patched here sets the module's polyphony.
Shifts the main oscillator's pitch by up to half an octave either way.
Shifts the pitch by a fifth of an octave per volt, added to FINE.
Sets where the main oscillator reads in the table, 0 giving the waveform captured at the top INPUT jack and 1 the one captured at the bottom jack, blending between them in between.
Adds a tenth of its voltage to POS, and the total is held between 0 and 1.
Turns oscillator 2 on and off; the lamp is lit while it is on, and switching it on restarts that oscillator.
MAIN restarts oscillator 2 at the beginning of every cycle of the main oscillator; OFF leaves it free-running.
Raises oscillator 2 above the main pitch, unison at the left through to a full octave at the right.
Raises oscillator 2 by a fifth of an octave per volt, added to its own DETUNE knob.
Offsets oscillator 2's reading position from the main POS, -1 to +1, and the total is held between 0 and 1.
Adds a tenth of its voltage to oscillator 2's position offset.
Turns oscillator 3 on and off; the lamp is lit while it is on, and switching it on restarts that oscillator.
MAIN restarts oscillator 3 on every cycle of the main oscillator; OSC 2 restarts it on every cycle of oscillator 2, and does nothing while oscillator 2 is off; OFF leaves it free-running.
Raises oscillator 3 above oscillator 2's pitch rather than above the main pitch, unison at the left through to a full octave at the right.
Raises oscillator 3 by a fifth of an octave per volt, added to its own DETUNE knob.
Offsets oscillator 3's reading position from the main POS, -1 to +1, and the total is held between 0 and 1.
Adds a tenth of its voltage to oscillator 3's position offset; the maker's tooltip names this jack as oscillator 2's.

Adds its voltage to that knob's weight, and the total is held between 0 and 10.
While this is patched the internal clock is switched off and a new value is drawn on each rising edge here.
Sets the rate of the internal clock in octaves around C4's 261.63Hz, -10 at the left through to +10 at the right.
Adds twice its voltage to RATE, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
Sets how long the output takes to travel from the old value to the new one, an instant jump at the left through to 1 second at the right.
Adds a tenth of its voltage to SMOOTH, and the total is held inside the knob's own range.
LIN travels between values at a steady rate; EXP follows a curve that starts slowly and finishes fast.
The generated voltage, -5V to +5V, travelling towards each new value at the rate SMOOTH sets.
Note — A newly placed module has RATE at its far right, which draws a new value several times per sample, so the output is noise until RATE is turned down or a clock is patched to TRIG.
Note — With SMOOTH at 0 the output steps straight to each new value, which makes the module a sample and hold on its own random source.
Note — The drawing between the knob rows is the current probability curve across the output range; it shows the weights and cannot be clicked or dragged.
Menu — Constant distribution (instead of linear) — gives every voltage inside one of the eight intervals the same chance, instead of sloping from one knob's weight to the next.
